explanation: Since $\det(e^{tX}) = e^{t\,\mathrm{tr}(X)}$, the group condition $\det = 1$ linearizes at the identity to $\mathrm{tr}\,A = 0$. Skew-symmetric matrices give $\mathfrak{so}_n$ and skew-Hermitian ones give $\mathfrak{u}_n$; invertibility is the defining condition of the group $GL_n$, not a linear condition cutting out a subalgebra.
